coverage_policy: Existing chapter/psalm spans remain conservative outer boundaries; proposed seams are metadata for B01 challenge, not promoted boundaries.

method.literary: Track prose/poetry shifts, speaker turns, headings, refrains, acrostics, collection seams, and embedded poems.
method.original_language: Flag Hebrew morphology, rare lexemes, parallelism, meter, acrostic letters, and superscription/heading scope; no lexical decision is asserted.
method.cross_reference: Record likely structural parallels only (e.g., Isa 36-39//2 Kgs; Jer 52//2 Kgs 24-25); defer semantic harmonization.
method.red_team: Challenge chapter-as-unit assumptions wherever speech, poem, refrain, acrostic, or narrative seams cross chapter boundaries.

Job: 3-31 speech cycles may cross chapter seams
28 is a bounded wisdom poem but rare Hebrew terms are disputed
38-42 poetry-to-prose and speaker/epilogue seams require challenge
Ps: Psalm-level units retained; superscriptions and internal stanzas are not silently normalized
alphabetic/acrostic and refrain structures require Hebrew evidence
collection seams (e.g., 72, 89, 106, 150) are candidate signals only
Prov: 1-9 extended instructions differ from aphoristic collections 10-29
30-31 speaker headings, numerical sayings, and acrostic poem require lexical review
Eccl: 3 time poem and 12 closing poem are embedded literary units
voice/frame and epilogue boundaries remain contested
refrain translations can hide structural recurrence
Song: speaker attribution, chorus/refrain, and scene shifts are unresolved
Hebrew imagery and compact lyric syntax make English segmentation unstable
Isa: 1-35 oracle cycles contain songs/woes/visions crossing chapters
36-39 is a narrative interlude with parallels in Kings
40-55 consolation and servant-song seams require challenge; 56-66 shifts to disputation/restoration
Jer: poetic oracles and prose narratives alternate irregularly
26-29, 30-33, 34-45, and 46-51 have collection/heading and chronology holds
52 is an appendix with a Kings parallel
Lam: 1-4 alphabetic acrostic/meter structures are evidence for stanza boundaries
Hebrew meter and rare terms remain unresolved

red_team_required_challenges: Reject any proposed seam justified only by English punctuation or chapter number.
Require an explicit speaker/heading/refrain/acrostic or discourse marker for a promoted internal seam.
Keep unresolved Hebrew ambiguity as a hold and preserve competing ranges in an appeal ledger.
Cross-reference only as a structural comparison; do not import chronology, authorship, or theology.
Verify exact coverage and no overlap after any future split or merge.
